themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in CD 308 surged to 14 THIS WEEK, up 250% from a 4-week baseline average of 4 complaints per week (z-score: 5.35), signaling a potential cluster of lead exposure incidents in housing stock that demands urgent investigation and resident notification.
evidence: 14 lead complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.35 indicates statistically rare spike
Crown Heights has older housing stock with known lead risk; children under 6 particularly vulnerable
No corresponding Reddit discussion or news coverage yet—early detection opportunity
reporting_angles: Map the 14 complaints geographically: Are they clustered in specific buildings or blocks? Interview residents and building owners.
Contact NYC Health Department to determine if they've detected a pattern; cross-reference with blood-lead screening data from local pediatricians and clinics.
Investigate whether recent renovations or demolitions (474 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 10 full demolitions) disturbed lead paint or pipes.

themes_detail.label: Dead and dying trees crisis
themes_detail.summary: Tree complaints exploded this week with 5 dead/dying tree reports (up 1233% from 0.4 weekly average) and 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints (up 700% from 0.6 weekly average), plus 6 new tree requests last week, suggesting either recent storm damage, neglect, or a coordinated inspection surge.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55)
5 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.29)
6 new tree requests filed last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 8.08)
Community board has repeated budget requests for park reconstruction/upgrades, indicating chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Was there a recent storm or weather event that triggered this spike? Cross-reference with National Weather Service data from the past 7-10 days.
Interview NYC Parks Department about tree maintenance schedules and budgets in CD 308; are crews responding to complaints?
Talk to residents about street tree conditions and canopy coverage; connect to broader environmental justice narrative about green space equity.

themes_detail.label: House of worship noise complaints
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship exploded to 4 last week, up 3100% from a near-zero baseline of 0.1 complaints per week (z-score: 11.72)—the single highest statistical anomaly in the dataset—pointing to either a new noise source or resident mobilization around a specific facility.
evidence: 4 house of worship noise complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 11.72 is highest statistical deviation in entire dataset, indicating unprecedented spike
Crown Heights has significant religious and cultural diversity; potential for interfaith or neighbor tension
No Reddit or news coverage yet; narrow window to investigate early
reporting_angles: Identify which house(s) of worship generated the 4 complaints; contact facility leadership and neighboring residents to understand dispute.
Determine if complaints are about prayer times, music, gatherings, or amplification; assess whether 311 complaints reflect broader neighborhood sentiment.
Interview NYPD and 311 about mediation options; explore whether community board has heard concerns or can facilitate dialogue.

themes_detail.label: Elevator outages in residential buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 3 last week, up 700% from a 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42), raising concerns about accessibility in multi-family housing and potential violations in buildings with disabled or elderly residents.
evidence: 3 elevator complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)
Heat/hot water complaints remain elevated at 1765 over 90 days, suggesting broader building maintenance issues
272 alteration permits filed in last 90 days; possible that renovations are disrupting elevators
No corresponding constituent cases or news coverage—signal may be under-reported by affected residents
reporting_angles: Identify the 3 buildings with complaints; verify elevator inspection records and complaint history via NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development.
Interview residents in affected buildings, especially elderly and disabled tenants, about access challenges and timeline to repair.
Investigate whether landlords are meeting legal repair timelines (typically 24-48 hours for elevators); assess fines or violations.

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Nine illegal tree damage complaints were filed 3 weeks ago (up 279% from 2.4 weekly average, z-score: 6.68), suggesting either deliberate property damage, contractor negligence during construction, or organized removal activity in the district.
evidence: 9 illegal tree damage complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.68)
Spike predates current dead/dying tree complaints by ~2 weeks, suggesting causal relationship
104 new building permits and 10 full demolitions filed in last 90 days—construction activity may be source
Convergence with overgrown tree complaints and tree requests suggests systemic tree management crisis
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 9 illegal tree damage complaints with DOB demolition and alteration permits; identify construction sites that may be responsible.
Interview NYC Parks Enforcement about how they investigate illegal tree damage and what penalties apply.
Determine if there are repeat offenders or patterns; assess whether contractor licensing/oversight is adequate.
